1. Branching Strategy: Trunk-Based Development
Apex practices Trunk-Based Development with short-lived feature branches to maximize integration velocity and minimize
merge debt:
main : The canonical production-deployable trunk. Direct pushes and force-pushes are strictly locked.
feature/<TICKET>-<description> : Feature branches branched from latest main (lifespan < 48 hours).
bugfix/<TICKET>-<description> : Standard defect remediation.
hotfix/<TICKET>-<description> : Critical production patch branching directly from main tag.
2. Conventional Commit Messages Specification
Commit messages must adhere to the Conventional Commits specification to facilitate automated changelog generation
and semantic versioning:
# Commit Message Format
<type>(<optional scope>): <description> [#TICKET-ID]
# Allowed Types:
# feat:     A new feature for the user
# fix:      A bug fix
# docs:     Documentation changes only
# refactor: Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
# test:     Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
# chore:    Build tasks, dependency bumps, or tool configuration
# Example:
feat(rag): implement hybrid sparse-dense vector retrieval [#APEX-1042]

4. Rebasing, Merge Conflicts, and Semantic Version Tagging
# Keep your local feature branch up to date with trunk via rebase
git checkout main && git pull origin main
git checkout feature/APEX-1042-hybrid-retrieval
git rebase main
# Semantic Release Tagging on main trunk
git tag -a v2.4.0 -m "Release v2.4.0: Knowledge Assistant RAG v2"
git push origin v2.4.0
